prompt.context: BackupCo is a data backup and disaster recovery company. Its primary headquarters is in Boston, its client services department is in South Carolina, and its development is split between Texas and Ukraine. To expand its product offerings, reach, and revenue, it is considering purchasing CloudCo, a cloud backup provider headquartered in Southern California.
prompt.question: Our firm has been hired to evaluate this potential acquisition. How would you begin considering this deal?

clarifying_info.q: What does BackupCo produce? What is data backup and disaster recovery?
clarifying_info.a: BackupCo produces physical backup appliances that sit on-site at client locations, as well as software that clients can deploy on their own devices. These products help protect data by duplicating emails, databases, sales data, etc. to alternate locations. It only sells B2B.

clarifying_info.q: Does BackupCo sell its products worldwide?
clarifying_info.a: BackupCo does $100 million worth of business in North America and the remainder of its business in EMEA and APAC.

exhibits.title: 2019 Revenue in Terabytes of Data Protected
exhibits.shows: A grouped bar chart showing CloudCo's quarterly terabytes of data protected by subscription tier (Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3) across Q1–Q4 of 2019. Note: 1TB = 1000GB.

exhibits.title: Post Acquisition Costs and Revenue Projections
exhibits.shows: A table showing post-acquisition synergy projections with two sections: Revenue Synergies (Revenue Increase Per Gigabyte Sold in 2019 by tier) and Cost Synergies (as % of Revenue Synergies for SG&A, Headcount, and R&D).

framework: Valuation: determine what CloudCo is worth on a standalone basis — consider DCF (preferred), comparable company analysis, and EBITDA multiples

Synergies: quantify revenue synergies (cross-sell, up-sell) and cost synergies (headcount reduction/relocation, scale, CAPEX reduction, R&D consolidation, shared IT/vendor/license costs) minus dis-synergies (lost customers, process breakdown)

Risk assessment: regulatory risk, key talent retention, loss of key customers, overly optimistic synergy estimates, culture clash, brand deterioration, vendor/cost relationship risks, extended integration timeline
Integration structure: propose an IMO/PMO-led structure with functional workstreams (Product, Finance/HR, Supply Chain, Engineering, Sales & Marketing) under an executive steering committee

questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize multiple valuation methods (DCF, comparables, EBITDA multiples) and be guided to a DCF. Candidate should ask for a hurdle rate. Candidate then requests cash flows and works through Exhibit 1 to compute annual profit, then applies the Gordon Growth perpetuity formula.

math.setup: Hurdle rate (WACC) = 13%; expected growth rate g = 3%. CloudCo sells three subscription tiers priced per GB per month. Annual profit = monthly profit x 12. Perpetuity value = CF / (WACC - g).
steps: Tier 1: 10 TB sold in Q4 = 10,000 GB. Price = $10/GB/month. Monthly profit = 10,000 x $10 = $100,000

Tier 2: 10 TB sold in Q4 = 10,000 GB... wait, use Q4 annual run-rate. Actually use full-year total: Q4 annualized. Per case guidance, use 10TB for Tier 1, 25TB for Tier 2, 40TB for Tier 3 (sum of all quarters per tier: Tier1=2+2+10+10=24... interviewer instructs to use 10/25/40 TB as the figures).
Using interviewer-provided figures: Tier 1 = 10 TB = 10,000 GB x $10 = $100,000/month

questions.prompt: Assuming a standalone valuation of $60M, how much should BackupCo be willing to pay for CloudCo?
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize that a strategic acquirer should be willing to pay up to standalone value PLUS captured synergies. Push candidate to think about synergy value. Provide Exhibit 2 when candidate moves in this direction. Candidate applies the same perpetuity formula to the total incremental profit (standalone CF + synergy CF).

math.setup: Use Exhibit 2 synergy figures. Revenue synergy = $1/GB increase across all tiers. Cost synergies are expressed as % of revenue synergy dollar amount. Use 10% discount rate (g assumed 0 for simplicity, or WACC-g=10% as before).
steps: Revenue synergy per month: Tier 1 = 10,000 GB x $1 = $10,000; Tier 2 = 25,000 GB x $1 = $25,000; Tier 3 = 40,000 GB x $1 = $40,000
Cost synergies (on $900,000): SG&A 10% = $90,000; Headcount 15% = $135,000; R&D 5% = $45,000; Total cost synergies = $270,000
math.answer: BackupCo should be willing to pay up to $71.7 million for CloudCo

questions.prompt: (Optional) We have been asked to develop a proposed M&A integration structure for BackupCo's acquisition. How might you design this?
questions.guidance: Candidate should sketch an org chart with: (1) Executive Steering Committee at the top, (2) Integration Management Office / PMO below, (3) functional workstreams beneath PMO: Product, Synergy Management Office, Finance/HR, Supply Chain, Engineering, Sales & Marketing. Organizing by function is preferred over organizing by territory for this type of technology company.

recommendation: BackupCo should look to purchase CloudCo for less than $71.7 million
Strong revenue and cost synergies, plus cross-sell and up-sell potential, make the acquisition very attractive
risks: Synergy estimates may be overly optimistic — validate against comparable prior transactions
Risk of losing key CloudCo customers during integration
Risk of losing key talent without a structured retention program
next_steps: Approach CloudCo to validate acquisition interest and obtain additional data needed to refine synergy estimates
